comments.body:
# RCA — store wedge that stranded local ticket events off origin (P0, RESOLVED — no permanent loss)

## Symptom
rebar ticket writes (incl. the akitainu completion attestation) were not reaching
`origin/tickets`. The shared local store sat **28 commits ahead / 125 behind** origin and
falling further behind; the akitainu close kept failing the completion-verifier gate because
its attestation never landed on origin.

## Proven root cause (two artifacts, one systemic defect)
**(1) Upstream — compaction leaves the tracker working tree dirty, non-atomically.**
`_compact_locked()` (`src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py:449-466`) writes `SNAPSHOT.json`,
renames sources to `*.retired`, and only *afterward* `git add -A` + commits; the lock releases
in `finally`. There is **no rollback** around the write/rename. Since `d2dea317ec` this runs in
a **detached background sweep** (`compact_trigger.py:287-318 _spawn_detached_sweep`) spawned from
the close. If that worker is SIGKILLed / times out / the parent exits after mutate-before-commit,
the working tree is left dirty: untracked `SNAPSHOT.json` + `*.retired` + `.tmp-event-*`, and
working-tree-deleted `.archived` files. Nothing runs `git checkout`/`git clean` on worker death.

**(2) Wedge — reconverge's union-merge cannot tolerate those untracked leftovers.**
`_union_merge` (`src/rebar/_store/sync.py:182-190`) runs `git merge origin/tickets`. Another
clone already compacted the *same* tickets and pushed those `.retired`/`SNAPSHOT` paths to
origin, so the merge must **create** those paths — but they already exist **untracked** in the
working tree → git aborts *"untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge."*
Failure handling is abort-only (`sync.py:191-197`); push-recovery `_recover_dirty_merge`
(`push_recovery.py:136-143`) uses `git reset --hard` (tracked-only, explicit *"untracked files
are left alone"*) and `_stash_create` (`push_recovery.py:55-68`, **no `-u`**), so it cannot clear
untracked files. Every retry re-aborts identically → permanent wedge → local commits never reach
origin, lost if the worktree is removed.

## Discriminating evidence / proof
- Reset/reconverge path exonerated: scanned all 33,621 reflog entries / 2,194 resets in the
  shared tracker — **0 unsafe resets** (every one a safe FF-adopt). Not the loss vector.
- Isolated runtime repro (`/tmp/mergerepro`): reproduced the exact `git merge` abort (exit 2);
  confirmed `git stash` **without** `-u` reports "No local changes to save" and does NOT rescue
  it; confirmed both `git stash -u` and `git clean` of the regenerable leftovers unblock the
  merge while preserving the unique local commit.
- Topology: ~90 `.tickets-tracker` dirs are separate worktrees sharing **one** `.git`
  (inode 976794618) → one HEAD (f36a24a9de) → one object store. One shared wedge surfaced at
  ~90 paths.

## defect_legitimacy = `defect`
Violates the non-destructive reconverge invariant stated in `sync.py`'s own header and the
AGENTS.md contract "the store shares every write immediately (auto-commit + auto-push)".

## Recovery performed (TOP priority — DONE, verified)
Under rebar's exclusive `write_lock(tracker)`: backed up + preserved all 232 untracked files
(incl. 6 `.tmp-event-*`), `git checkout -- .` (restored 115 deleted `.archived`), removed the
regenerable untracked leftovers, `git merge origin/tickets` (union), verified **all 28** stranded
event files present (incl. akitainu attestation `55cb8610`), pushed to origin.
**Result: ahead=0 / behind=0; attestation + all 28 events on origin; tree clean; live write
round-trip confirmed.**

## No permanent data loss
The 6 orphaned `.tmp-event-*` were triaged: 2 were prior-session debug probes; the other 4
(a REVIEW_RESULT PASS, a regression COMMENT, two description EDITs) each have their content
already committed on origin under a **retry uuid** (superseding review PASS on `06e0`; comment +
edit on `0d15`; edit on `e30d`). Every stranded write reached origin via retry. Backup retained
at the recorded /tmp path until fully closed out.

## Out of scope (separate products, not this store)
`parity-scan/.tickets-tracker` → `github.com/navapbc/flex-parity-scan`;
`digital-service-orchestra/.tickets-tracker` → its own repo. Both are different products' stores
(may share the bug class); not touched. d-s-o had ahead=0 (no loss).

## Fix plan (secondary priority — see description)
Primary: make reconverge/push-recovery robust to stale untracked leftovers (relocate/clean
colliding untracked paths before the union merge). Defense-in-depth: make compaction crash-atomic
(roll back the dirty tree on worker death). RED→GREEN, held-out oracle + mutation check; land via
Gerrit.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Compaction can leave the tracker working tree dirty (untracked `SNAPSHOT.json` / `*.retired`
regenerated by a peer clone and pushed to origin). The next reconverge runs
`git merge origin/tickets` in `src/rebar/_store/sync.py::_union_merge`; because origin now wants
to CREATE those same paths, git aborts with *"untracked working tree files would be overwritten
by merge."* The handler is abort-only (`sync.py:191-197`) and push-recovery cannot clear
untracked files (`push_recovery.py`: `git reset --hard` is tracked-only; `_stash_create` omits
`-u`). Every retry re-aborts → the store wedges, stranding local commits off origin. Proven end
to end (RCA comment on this ticket; runtime repro `/tmp/mergerepro`).

## Fix (primary — breaks the wedge at the proven site)
Make the union merge self-heal the ONE recoverable abort class: untracked paths that origin is
about to introduce. In `_union_merge`, when `git merge` fails, detect the
"untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge" signature and parse the exact paths
git names. Relocate ONLY those named untracked paths into a quarantine directory under the git
common dir (`<git-common-dir>/reconverge-quarantine/<utc-ts>/`, OUTSIDE any worktree so they
cannot re-collide), then retry the merge once.
- On retry success: origin's authoritative committed versions are now present; the union keeps
  both parents, so no local commit is orphaned. Quarantine is retained as a safety copy (not
  deleted inline).
- On any other failure or a genuine content conflict: fall back to today's behavior exactly —
  `git merge --abort`, keep local, log the `rebar fsck-recover` hint.

### Why this is safe / non-destructive
- Only the paths git explicitly names are moved, and that error names ONLY files that already
  exist on origin (that is WHY they collide) — i.e. regenerable compaction artifacts.
- `.tmp-event-*` real uncommitted event-appends live at the tracker ROOT and do not exist on
  origin, so git never names them → they are never quarantined.
- Files are MOVED, never deleted, so even a mistaken selection loses nothing.

## Portability
In-process; uses only local `git`. No CI-provider trigger, no network dependency — the recovery
runs wherever reconverge runs (satisfies `project.portability`).

## file_impact
- `src/rebar/_store/sync.py` — add untracked-collision quarantine+retry to `_union_merge`; add a
  small parser for the git error's path list and a quarantine helper.
- `tests/unit/test_store_sync_reconverge.py` (new) — RED→GREEN coverage.

## Test plan (RED→GREEN, held-out oracle)
1. RED: construct a tracker whose HEAD lacks a path that `origin/tickets` adds, and place that
   same path as an UNTRACKED file in the working tree; call the reconverge entry; assert it
   currently raises/leaves HEAD un-merged (the abort). Confirm it fails for the untracked-overwrite
   reason (not an unrelated error).
2. GREEN after fix: same fixture → merge completes, HEAD contains both parents, the local-only
   commit remains reachable, and the quarantined copy exists.
3. Mutation check: re-introduce the abort-only handler (skip the quarantine) → test returns RED.
4. Refactoring litmus: assertions are on observable git state (HEAD parents, reachability, files),
   not private names.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A reconverge whose union merge would abort ONLY on origin-introduced untracked paths now
      completes, keeping both parents; no local commit orphaned.
- [ ] A genuine content conflict still aborts, keeps local, and hints `rebar fsck-recover`
      (unchanged behavior).
- [ ] `.tmp-event-*` and any untracked path NOT named by git are left untouched.
- [ ] New unit test is legitimately RED before the fix and GREEN after; mutation returns it to RED.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean; change lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1 AND
      Verified +1) before this ticket closes.

## Defense-in-depth (separate follow-up, linked discovered_from)
Make compaction crash-atomic (roll back the dirty tree if the detached sweep dies before commit)
so the dirty state is not produced in the first place. Not required to stop the loss — the
reconverge self-heal above already breaks the wedge — so tracked as a linked follow-up, not this
ticket's scope.

file_impact.reason: add untracked-collision quarantine+retry to _union_merge so reconverge self-heals instead of wedging
new RED->GREEN test for the untracked-overwrite recovery

compiled_state.title: Compaction leaves tracker working tree dirty; reconverge union-merge then wedges store (untracked-overwrite abort), stranding local ticket events off origin
